name: Ventricular System, CSF Circulation and Hydrocephalus

reference.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students / Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy
clinicalPearls: CSF is produced by choroid plexus in lateral, third and fourth ventricles at ~500 mL/day (~0.35 mL/min); total volume is ~150 mL
Foramina of Monro connect lateral ventricles to third ventricle; aqueduct of Sylvius connects third to fourth ventricle
Fourth ventricle exits into subarachnoid space via median foramen of Magendie and two lateral foramina of Luschka
Arachnoid granulations absorb CSF into superior sagittal sinus; absorption rate is pressure-dependent
Normal pressure hydrocephalus triad (Hakim-Adams triad): gait disturbance (magnetic gait), urinary incontinence, dementia (Wet, Wobbly, Wacky)
reference.pathophysiology: Obstruction of ventricular pathways causes non-communicating (obstructive) hydrocephalus, most frequently at the narrow cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius (aqueductal stenosis) or fourth ventricle outlets. Impaired absorption by scarred arachnoid villi following subarachnoid hemorrhage or purulent meningitis produces communicating hydrocephalus. Overproduction by choroid plexus papilloma is rare.
additionalInvestigations: Brain MRI with 3D CISS/FIESTA for aqueductal patency and Evans index (>0.30 confirms ventriculomegaly)
High-volume lumbar puncture (tap test: 30-50 mL CSF removal) demonstrating gait improvement in NPH
Continuous intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring with B-waves
